Cost and loop reliability

'Citations dropped' counts PMIDs whose real PubMed title did not match the title the model claimed -- i.e. fabricated or mis-attributed references caught by verification. 'Quote flags' are concentration quotes the model claimed were verbatim but that were not found in the cited abstract. 'Eligibility flags' are spectroscopic category labels, macromolecules at whole-molecule molarity, or duplicates that survived the retry loop. 'Robust' detectable candidates still clear the threshold at the LOW corner of the literature concentration range x reference k_ex spread; 'fragile' ones clear it only at the point estimate.

'Field-strength coverage' is the share of (metabolite x field strength) pairs with a simulation result; since the deterministic stage took over, a gap means the metabolite had no exchangeable group with a verified reference exchange rate (reported as unknown), not a skipped tool call. 'Undifferentiated' means the experimentalist gave a metabolite the same concentration in every ROI, which defeats the ROI-differential scan design. 'Protocol arithmetic problems' checks that the pulse train adds up to the stated saturation time, that saturation fits inside the TR, and that the stated duty cycle matches the pulse timing.

Candidate overlap: detectability, best contrast, concentration used

How the fields are chosen: no model decides what to test. Every proton group with a verified reference rate is swept over B1 x Tsat at ALL of 0.5, 1.5, 3, 5, 7 T, and the metabolite is 'detectable' when its best group reaches >= 0.5% with-vs-without contrast at any of them. A cell's headline ('@ 5 T') is only the field with the highest contrast; the bracket lists the contrast at every field so a 'no @ 5 T' means below threshold everywhere, not untested elsewhere. 'unknown' means no group of that candidate had a verified reference rate, so nothing was simulated at any field. Because the simulator is shared, a different contrast for the same metabolite means the models fed it different concentrations, shifts or group classes.

One row per model, pooling its replicate runs. 'Citation drop rate' is dropped / (kept + dropped) over all agents and runs. 'Replicate candidate Jaccard' is the overlap of candidate sets between two runs of the SAME model (1.0 = identical candidate lists), the yardstick against which between-model Jaccard values in the pairwise table should be read; 'n/a' with one run. A between-model difference smaller than the within-model spread is noise.

Cross-run consensus per candidate

How many independent runs and models converge on each candidate, and on its detectability. Agreement across models and replicates is stronger evidence than any single run; a candidate one run alone proposes, or that is detectable in one of several replicates of the same model, should be read as unstable.

k_ex and shift come from the reference table keyed by the chemist's group class; the model chooses only the class. 'Borrowed' means no measurement in the requested tissue exists in the table and the provenance names the tissue/species/phantom it was taken from. A status other than 'simulated' means the pipeline said 'unknown' rather than inventing a value.

  • 9-9 replicate runs per model. Local-model runs are stochastic (sampling at the model's default temperature); read the between-model differences against the within-model spread in the per-model summary (replicate Jaccard and detectability agreement), and treat a candidate proposed in only one replicate as unstable.
